items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: in 1912 he had a ragtime piece, song, published by Grunewald there, Baby C, see.

ctx.x: I think it was Tony's tune. But now, I will have to admit that up to the time I last heard Tony, I heard him play very few Bruce, and I heard him sing no Bruce songs. See, he played some of that kind of music, little snatches of it. But he never, he never sang any Bruce songs. He sang mostly popular songs, and he had a couple of instrumental pieces of his own that he played, probably more than that, but two of them he wrote up and tried to get them published in town and they wouldn't publish them. Offered him $5…

items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: I didn't know Baby Seals, but he had a couple of pieces published in New Orleans

ctx.x: Honey Baby. As you remember, it was the familiar blues chords.

It had blues chords in it, blues notes in it. But it didn't stick strictly to the 12 bars. You might have, you might have called it a 14 bar maybe, or you, but it didn't stand strictly with that, the 12 bar as the, as it was afterwards the, the Orthodox real country blues was a 12 bar thing that they, that they held it to. But it did have the blue notes in it. And I asked him, I wrote Kennedy and asked him, he was in New York at the time, I wrote and asked him when he had arranged it. He said it was several years…
called Baby Seals Blues, which was... Was that a, what you might call a traditional blues?
